papers.title: Immortal Time-Bias-Corrected Survival of Highly Sensitized Patients and HLA-desensitized Kidney Transplant Recipients.
papers.one_line: Compares survival of desensitized and non-desensitized kidney transplant recipients against patients still waitlisted using a time-varying covariate model, and finds no difference where uncorrected comparisons in this field show a transplant advantage.
papers.what_was_done: All patients at one French transplant centre on the waiting list between August 1994 and December 2019 with panel-reactive antibodies of 80 percent or more were included, 326 in total, of whom 147 remained waitlisted at last follow-up and 179 were transplanted, including 36 desensitized of whom 30 were transplanted. All-cause mortality was the primary outcome. A time-varying covariate Cox model was used to handle the immortal time inherent to comparing transplanted patients against those still waiting, since the transplanted did not die between listing and transplantation by definition, with a landmark analysis as sensitivity analysis. There were no differences in mortality between desensitized recipients, non-desensitized recipients and waitlisted patients, with a hazard ratio of 0.48 and a p value of 0.22, and death-censored graft survival was similar between desensitized and non-desensitized recipients after adjusting for donor age, donor status and waiting time. Estimated glomerular filtration rate at one year was 53.3 against 53.6 millilitres per minute. The paper notes that a comparison study matched waitlist controls on having survived a similar waiting time, which prevents generalization to the whole listed cohort, and that its own longer waiting times for deceased-donor recipients could overestimate their death risk.

future_research.gap: Follow-up may be too short, and significantly shorter in the desensitized group, to detect chronic antibody-mediated rejection and transplant glomerulopathy.
future_research.quote: However, the duration of follow-up in our study may not have been long enough and is significantly shorter in the desensitized KT group to determine whether desensitized patients had a greater risk of chronic ABMR and transplant glomerulopathy.

problems.evidence: Comparing transplanted against waitlisted patients is immortal time by construction, since being transplanted requires surviving to the transplant, and the paper states this is inherent to every study evaluating desensitization on survival. Correcting it removes the survival advantage the uncorrected comparison would produce, and the paper presents this as the first time the comparison has been made with the bias accounted for.
problems.quote: Indeed, in the field of KT, the immortal time bias induces a survival advantage to KT patients, as compared to patients still on waiting list, because they de facto did not die during the period between the inscription and the transplantation.

problems.evidence: A comparison study handled the same problem by restricting waitlist controls to patients who had survived on the list for a time similar to the desensitized group's waiting time. That removes the immortal interval by conditioning on survival, and this paper identifies the cost: the comparison no longer generalizes to the population of listed patients, and it offers this as an explanation for why the two studies report different desensitization effects.
problems.quote: In the study by Manook et al. , 10 the waiting-list control group was matched to the desensitized group by focusing on nondesensitized patients having survived on the waiting list a time similar to the waiting time of desensitized patients. This prevents generalization to the whole cohort of patients registered on the waiting list.

papers.title: Medications and the Risk of Colorectal Cancer in Patients with Inflammatory Bowel Diseases: Use of the Landmark Method.
papers.one_line: Applies six landmark points to a national inflammatory bowel disease cohort and finds a drug's apparent protective effect against colorectal cancer present at one landmark and absent at the others.
papers.what_was_done: Using Korean national health insurance data, patients newly diagnosed with inflammatory bowel disease from 2006 to 2010 were followed for colorectal cancer to 2015, with 71 cancers among 6,452 Crohn's disease patients and 151 among 16,769 ulcerative colitis patients. A standard Cox model adjusted for confounders gave a 0.47-fold risk with immunomodulators in Crohn's disease and a 0.18-fold risk with 5-aminosalicylic acid in ulcerative colitis, both consistent with the published literature. Landmark analyses were then run at points from six months to three years. For Crohn's disease none of the landmark models reached significance. For ulcerative colitis the protective effect was significant at the six-month landmark and at none of the remaining five. The paper addresses a common defense directly: researchers sometimes assume that an immortal period much shorter than total follow-up has negligible effect, and here 57 percent of Crohn's patients received their first immunomodulator within a year of a ten-year follow-up, yet a six-month landmark changed the conclusion. It cites a chronic obstructive pulmonary disease study where the effect was significant at a three-month landmark and not at 6, 9 or 12 months, and lists what should inform the choice of landmark: treatment effect strength, sample size reduction, risk change over time, natural course, censoring proportion and follow-up length.

future_research.gap: The landmark method is not the only control for immortal time, and comparison against time-varying Cox models is left to future work.
future_research.quote: Moreover, the landmark method is not the only means with which to control immortal time bias. Future studies will need to evaluate other methods, such as time-varying Cox models, and compare them with the landmark method.

problems.evidence: Six landmark points on one dataset yield one significant result and five null ones for the same drug and outcome, and the paper's own recommendation is that consistent criteria free of the researcher's subjective involvement are needed for setting them. That is the entry's claim stated as a requirement the field does not meet: the parameter determining the conclusion is currently chosen by the analyst, and the paper's fallback is to report multiple landmarks as a sensitivity analysis.
problems.quote: Therefore, consistent criteria without subjective involvement of the researchers are necessary when setting the landmark points.

problems.evidence: Every landmark discards the patients who had the outcome or died before it, and the list of considerations the paper gives for choosing one includes sample size reduction alongside the substantive factors. With 71 and 151 cancers over a decade in a national cohort, moving the landmark later trades bias against the events that carry the estimate, and the paper offers no rule for making that trade.
problems.quote: Additionally, the strength of the treatment effect, sample size reduction, risk change over time, natural course of the disease, proportion of censored data, and length of follow-up should be considered. 26

papers.title: Penalized regression for left-truncated and right-censored survival data.
papers.one_line: Fits a penalized Cox model that adjusts for left truncation in high-dimensional clinico-genomic data, and shows that the concordance index cannot distinguish a model that mimics the data-generating process from one that does not.
papers.what_was_done: High-dimensional patient data force feature selection or penalization, and cohorts assembled at a milestone such as genomic testing are left-truncated, since patients entered the database only after diagnosis and after being at risk for some time. Penalized survival methods that adjust for left truncation are not commonly implemented. The paper applies a penalized Cox model for left-truncated and right-censored data and compares it against penalized models for right censoring alone, using simulations and a real clinico-genomic database of stage IV lung cancer. Models failing to adjust for left truncation overestimate true survival probabilities, while adjusted models are well calibrated even in high dimensions, and coefficient estimates differed significantly between the two in the real data. The direction of bias in a coefficient depends on the sign of that predictor's association with the truncation time: predictors positively associated with truncation time are biased downward because they carry more immortal time. Year of diagnosis moved from the largest coefficient in absolute value to below one after adjustment. The concordance index could not distinguish the correct model from the incorrect one, and was in part driven by correlation between predictors and left truncation, so the paper recommends evaluating with calibration as well as discrimination. It notes that temporal selection, where testing is ordered for worse-prognosis patients, can survive the truncation adjustment.

future_research.gap: Left truncation adjustment does not handle temporal selection, where the truncation time is itself correlated with survival because testing is ordered selectively.
future_research.quote: The latter may occur if left truncation time is correlated with survival time, for example, if genomic testing is ordered selectively for patients with worse prognosis.

problems.evidence: The standard performance metric for a survival model is blind to the failure that matters here: the concordance index could not distinguish a model reproducing the data-generating process from one that did not, and in the real data was inflated by correlation between predictors and the truncation time. An analyst optimizing predictive discrimination would therefore have selected the wrong model and read its performance as good, which is the disconnection between prediction quality and structural correctness the entry describes.
problems.quote: For example, our simulations suggest that the commonly used C‐index cannot differentiate between models that mimic the true data generating process and those that do not, and may therefore lead to misleading conclusions in the presence of LTRC data.

problems.evidence: For cohorts assembled at a milestone such as genomic testing, the paper supplies a penalized estimator that puts each patient into the risk set only from their actual entry, which is the correct handling of delayed entry in high dimensions and was not previously available. It also gives the rule for reading an unadjusted result: the bias in each coefficient follows the sign of its association with the truncation time, so year of diagnosis reversed direction on adjustment. It covers delayed entry rather than the choice of time origin, and does not address selection into testing.
problems.quote: In particular, our simulation shows that predictions from models that fail to adjust for left truncation will overestimate true survival probabilities whereas models that properly adjust can yield well calibrated survival predictions, even with high‐dimensional data.

problems.evidence: In a clinico-genomic database the covariates include mutation features, and the paper shows the estimates are shaped by how patients came to be in the database at all: variants in EGFR and ALK appeared protective, which it attributes to those mutations qualifying patients for targeted therapy rather than to any direct effect. A learned high-dimensional representation of such a database therefore encodes treatment eligibility and referral, not only biology.
problems.quote: Conversely, variants in EGFR and ALK were found to be protective in the CGDB data, putatively because mutations in these genes qualify patients to receive targeted therapies and therefore benefit from improved response and longer survival.

papers.title: Bilateral Salpingo-oophorectomy and Breast Cancer Risk for BRCA1 and BRCA2 Mutation Carriers: Assessing the Evidence.
papers.one_line: Reviews twenty years of observational evidence on whether risk-reducing oophorectomy lowers breast cancer risk in BRCA carriers, finding the early protective results were produced by biases that contemporary studies have reduced without reaching agreement.
papers.what_was_done: Risk-reducing bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy clearly reduces tubo-ovarian cancer risk in BRCA1 and BRCA2 carriers; whether it reduces breast cancer risk is the question, and it matters because several international guidelines recommend considering premenopausal surgery for that purpose. No randomized trial exists or is thought feasible, since women would not accept randomization. The review sets out the biases in the early studies that produced the protective association, immortal person-time bias, confounding by indication, informative censoring and confounding by other risk factors, and then assesses seven contemporary studies designed to reduce some of them. Of four studies of premenopausal surgery in BRCA1 carriers, using population average age at menopause as a surrogate for menopausal status, only one showed a clear protective association while the other three gave hazard ratios between 0.84 and 1.11 with intervals covering one. All four studies in BRCA2 carriers gave point estimates below one, from 0.17 to 0.77, but only one excluded the null, and that one counted only breast cancers before age 50. The review concludes the evidence does not support recommending premenopausal surgery for breast cancer risk reduction, and that residual bias likely persists in the contemporary studies.

future_research.gap: An individual participant data meta-analysis might resolve whether the consistently sub-unit BRCA2 estimates reflect an underpowered real effect, but would not remove the residual confounding and bias.
future_research.quote: An individual participant data meta-analysis may help to clarify this point, although the problem of residual confounding and bias will not be overcome by meta-analytic techniques.

problems.evidence: The review states that some of these biases cannot be fully mitigated in an observational design at all, and that confounding by indication has mitigation strategies so demanding that applying them would severely limit the sample size. That is the trade the entry describes without a workflow: the devices that would address the residual confounding are available in principle and cost the study its power, so twenty years of evidence remains inconclusive on a question guiding surgical decisions.
problems.quote: Some biases cannot be fully mitigated in an observational study design, and others, such as confounding by indication, have mitigation strategies that are very difficult to achieve without severely limiting the sample size.

problems.evidence: A protective association strong enough to enter international guidelines arose from designs the review now identifies as carrying immortal person-time among other biases, and the contemporary studies built to reduce those biases do not reproduce it. The exposure is a surgery that can happen at any age, so the interval from cohort entry to surgery is time the woman had to survive cancer-free, and the guidelines built on the earlier result remain in place.
problems.quote: However, these historical studies were hampered by the presence of several important biases, including immortal person-time bias, confounding by indication, informative censoring, and confounding by other risk factors, which may have led to overestimation of any protective benefit.

problems.evidence: Any protective effect would be biologically confined to premenopausal surgery, since surgery after menopause does not change circulating hormone levels, and menopausal status was not observed in these studies. The population average age at menopause was substituted, so the strategy actually contrasted is surgery before or after a fixed age rather than before or after menopause, and the one study reaching significance further restricted the outcome to cancers before age 50.
problems.quote: Of the four studies ( 5, 8–10 ) that assessed the association between premenopausal rrBSO and breast cancer risk in BRCA1 mutation carriers (using the average age of menopause in the general population, 50 or 51 years, as a surrogate for actual menopausal status), only Stjepanovic and colleagues ( 10 ) showed a clear protective association.

papers.title: Immortal Time Bias in Comparing Late vs Early Intubation in Patients With Coronavirus Disease 2019.
papers.one_line: Letter showing that a reported association between late intubation and longer intensive care stay is produced by counting the pre-intubation interval as part of the stay, and arguing the admission date does not mark a common disease stage.
papers.what_was_done: A study had compared late against early intubation in COVID-19 and found late intubation associated with longer intensive care stay and longer mechanical ventilation. The letter accepts the physiological explanation as plausible and identifies a design explanation as well: the interval from admission to intubation is immortal time during which death cannot occur, and when length of stay is measured from admission that interval is attributed to the effect of intubation, lengthening the stay in the late group by construction. Three remedies are proposed. Resetting time zero to the moment of intubation is defended on the substantive ground that intubation criteria are applied uniformly within an institution, so intubation marks a comparable physiological state, whereas admission does not, since some patients arrive early in their illness and others late. A Cox model with intubation as a time-varying covariate would allow adjustment for other time-varying confounders. And time-dependent propensity score matching would accommodate the varying probability of intubation over the hospital stay, which the letter notes matters because the original study states that intubation was decided by the treating physician without explicit criteria.

problems.evidence: The exposure is defined by when an intervention happened and the outcome is measured from a different origin, so the exposure contrast partly measures the gap between the two clocks. The letter's substantive point is sharper than the arithmetic one: admission does not correspond to a common point in the disease because patients present at different stages, so no correction that keeps admission as time zero puts the arms on a comparable footing.
problems.quote: In contrast, the time of admission may not represent the same stage of coronavirus disease 2019. In other words, some patients may arrive at the hospital at an early stage, but others may arrive at a late stage.

problems.evidence: The original study states that intubation was determined by the treating physician without explicit criteria, so the probability of being intubated varies across patients and over the stay according to unrecorded clinical judgment. The letter's proposed remedy is a time-dependent propensity score, which models that probability from what was recorded and leaves the judgment itself unmeasured.
problems.quote: Because the authors have stated that the intubation is determined by the treating physician without explicit criteria, the propensity of receiving intubation varied across patients during the hospital stay.

papers.title: Methodological frontiers in vaccine safety: qualifying available evidence for rare events, use of distributed data networks to monitor vaccine safety issues, and monitoring the safety of pregnancy interventions.
papers.one_line: Reviews what postmarketing vaccine safety assessment can and cannot do for rare events and in pregnancy, and argues that the evidence-grading criteria which downgrade observational data should themselves be reconsidered.
papers.what_was_done: Licensing trials are too small to detect rare adverse events and generally exclude pregnant women, so postmarketing safety rests on observational data. The review covers three fronts. For rare events, large linked databases, distributed data networks and case-centred methods have enabled study, while many countries including most low- and middle-income ones lack such databases, so vaccines used only there cannot be assessed this way; case-only methods are efficient but need an unbiased set of cases with linked vaccination records, and coded events with non-specific symptoms and unclear onset have low positive predictive value while validation may be impossible or expensive. Distributed networks require common protocols, definitions, data models and analytics, and privacy-preserving methods, and need sustained funding rather than ad hoc assembly. Safety in pregnancy is complicated by physiological change, mother-child linkage and long-term infant follow-up, with differential access to and use of antenatal care, immortal time bias, seasonal timing of pregnancy and unmeasured determinants of pregnancy outcomes named as potential biases that have yet to be fully explored. The review notes that available appraisal tools downgrade observational evidence relative to trials, and argues for rebalancing on the ground that there is no single gold standard.

future_research.gap: The biases affecting studies of vaccine exposure during pregnancy, including immortal time and seasonal timing, have not been fully explored and the methods to address them are undeveloped.
future_research.quote: Potential sources of bias including differential access to and utilisation of antenatal care, immortal time bias, seasonal timing of pregnancy and unmeasured determinants of pregnancy outcomes have yet to be fully explored.

future_research.gap: Whether bias analysis or validation of a subset of cases is the better route for events with low positive predictive value is unresolved.
future_research.quote: Further work on bias analysis would be beneficial in this area as well as the merits of validation on subsets of cases.
future_research.locator: Detection, power, specificity, bias and delayed onset

problems.evidence: The outcome in a vaccine safety study is a coded event, and the review states that for events with non-specific symptoms and unclear onset the positive predictive value is low while validation may be impossible or too expensive. It then poses the open question directly: what it means methodologically to assess events where specificity is lacking, and whether bias analysis or partial validation is the answer. The error is therefore known to be present, unquantified, and without an agreed route to quantification.
problems.quote: While some adverse events are well diagnosed and coded in records, others may have non-specific symptoms with unclear onset meaning coded events have a low positive predictive value.
problems.locator: Detection, power, specificity, bias and delayed onset

problems.evidence: The appraisal tools that determine whether postmarketing evidence is acted on downgrade observational data by construction, and the review proposes reconsidering the criteria rather than meeting them. That is the absence of a threshold seen from the other side: no rule states what an observational vaccine safety study would have to show to count, only a rule that it counts for less than a trial.
problems.quote: It may be time to re-evaluate the GRADE criteria themselves and provide more balance in our evaluation of available evidence.

problems.evidence: Studying events too rare for one population requires pooling across networks, and the review states that this requires harmonisation of protocols, data models, definitions and analytics as a precondition rather than a consequence. Assessment in pregnancy adds a further requirement, common data models prioritising mother-child linkage and recording that permits accurate timing of exposure within pregnancy, which existing sources do not supply.
problems.quote: This requires sustainable networks employing CDMs that prioritise mother-child linkage and recording of variables which allow for accurate ascertainment of the timing of exposure during pregnancy.

papers.title: New-user and prevalent-user designs and the definition of study time origin in pharmacoepidemiology: A review of reporting practices.
papers.one_line: Reviews 89 pharmacoepidemiologic cohort studies and finds 40 percent used a new-user design in both arms, with eligibility, initiation and start of follow-up reported as aligned in 53 percent of those.
papers.what_was_done: Guidance recommends the new-user design because it reduces selection bias relative to a prevalent-user design, and the review asks how far that has been taken up and, going further, whether the studies that use it actually align the three times. Eighty-nine observational effectiveness and safety cohort studies published in six pharmacoepidemiological journals in 2018 and 2019 were reviewed with a purpose-built extraction tool. Forty percent reported a new-user design in both the exposure and comparator arms and 13 percent a prevalent-user design in both, with three studies giving a rationale for including prevalent users. Among those reporting a new-user design, the moment of meeting eligibility criteria, treatment initiation and start of follow-up were reported as aligned in both arms in 53 percent. The review gives examples of studies that minimized the risk from an unclear time origin in unexposed participants, from immortal time, and from a time lag. It states that the review is the first to examine implementation in terms of alignment rather than in terms of whether new or prevalent users were included, and that the implications of misalignment were difficult to assess because assessing them would require the target estimand to be reported explicitly.

future_research.gap: The consequence of misaligning the time origin cannot be judged without the target estimand being reported, which the original studies did not do.
future_research.quote: Implications of misalignment of study design origin were difficult to assess because it would require explicit reporting of the target estimand in original studies.

problems.evidence: Adopting the recommended design is not the same as achieving what the design is for. Of the studies reporting a new-user design in both arms, roughly half reported the three times as aligned, so the label and the property come apart in about half of the compliant studies, and the review notes it is the first to look past the label at the alignment.
problems.quote: The moment of meeting eligibility criteria, treatment initiation, and start of follow‐up were reported to be aligned in both treatment arms in 53% of studies that reported implementing a new‐user design.

problems.evidence: The reviewers could not determine what the misalignments cost, because working that out requires knowing what quantity each study was trying to estimate, and the studies did not say. So the estimand is missing from the published record in a way that blocks not just interpretation of a result but assessment of whether its design was valid.
problems.quote: We recommend that the choice for a particular study time origin is explicitly motivated to enable assessment of validity of the study.

papers.title: Sampling designs for rare time-dependent exposures: a comparison of the nested exposure case-control design and exposure density sampling.
papers.one_line: Compares two sampling designs that estimate hazard ratios for rare time-dependent exposures from all exposed individuals and a small fraction of the unexposed, avoiding immortal time by construction while cutting the covariate ascertainment burden.
papers.what_was_done: Full-cohort analyses of hospital-acquired infection require covariate information on everyone, which is expensive, and the exposure is time-dependent, which conventional sampling designs for rare outcomes do not handle. The paper revisits and compares two designs built for rare time-dependent exposures with possibly common outcomes: the nested exposure case-control design and exposure density sampling. Both sample all exposed individuals and only a fraction of the unexposed, and both stratify on the risk set so that time-dependent exposure is respected and immortal time avoided. They are evaluated on patients in a neuro-intensive care unit in Moscow across three hospital-acquired infections of differing prevalence, and both are extended so that combined and competing endpoints can be analyzed against the full cohort while requiring substantially less information. Exposure density sampling outperformed the nested design on efficiency and accuracy in most settings, with smaller standard errors for fewer reference patients, though the nested design used substantially fewer controls where both the outcome and the exposure were rare. Inflation factors quantifying the power lost relative to the full cohort are derived, with the expression for the nested design given for the first time, and the paper notes the exposure density factors are somewhat optimistic and the nested ones conservative against the empirical values. Computing code and the dataset are released.

future_research.gap: Combining these designs with propensity score adjusted matching would allow reference groups differing only in exposure and is proposed for future application.
future_research.quote: In future applications, this adjusted sampling enables comparable control/reference groups that differ only for the exposure and can account for additional confounders.

problems.evidence: Both designs sample controls from the risk set at each exposure time, so the comparison is made among people still at risk when the exposure occurred and the immortal interval never enters. The timing is handled by the sampling structure rather than by a landmark or a correction, and the same structure handles competing endpoints. It applies where the exposure is rare and time-dependent and an unexposed reference exists at each event time, not to strategies indistinguishable at baseline.
problems.quote: Finally, we conclude that both designs are attractive alternatives to the full cohort analysis. They are both flexible designs that consider the most commonly observed biases: immortal time bias and competing risks bias.

problems.evidence: The registry entry says large databases yield small effective samples once the design restrictions are applied. These designs work the other way: they retain every exposed person and sample the unexposed, so the information about the contrast is preserved while the ascertainment cost falls, and the paper quantifies the resulting power loss against the full cohort with inflation factors, giving the expression for the nested design for the first time. The factors are approximate, optimistic for one design and conservative for the other.
problems.quote: We present IFs, that roughly quantify the loss of statistical power of NECC or, respectively, EDS compared to the full cohort.

problems.evidence: Both the computing code and the analyzed dataset are published, the code as supplementary material and the data in a public repository with a citable identifier. For a methods comparison whose conclusions depend on which design wins under which prevalence, that is the artifact set needed to check the comparison rather than accept it.
problems.quote: Computing code is available as Supplementary Material. The dataset analyzed during the current study is available in the Zenodo repository, https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.3995319 .

papers.title: Methodological evaluation of bias in observational coronavirus disease 2019 studies on drug effectiveness.
papers.one_line: Assesses eleven observational COVID-19 drug effectiveness studies published in four leading journal families and finds every one susceptible to immortal time, confounding or competing risk bias in its primary analysis.
papers.what_was_done: A PubMed search on 23 October 2020 identified observational cohort studies of drug effectiveness in hospitalized COVID-19 patients published in the British Medical Journal, New England Journal of Medicine, Journal of the American Medical Association and The Lancet and their sub-journals. Of 255 articles screened, 11 were evaluated against three pitfalls in time-to-event analysis. All 11 were susceptible to at least one in their primary analysis. Eight had a time-dependent treatment whose hazard ratios were not adjusted for immortal time in the primary analysis. Nine addressed baseline confounders, while time-varying confounding from time-varying treatment and clinical variables was less recognized. Only one of the 11 addressed competing event bias, by extending follow-up beyond discharge. The review recommends a stepwise analysis presenting simple and extended models side by side, beginning with a complete competing risk analysis giving cause-specific Cox models for the event of interest and for every competing event, then extending to propensity score methods and to g-methods for time-varying confounding. It discourages Kaplan-Meier plots where competing risks exist, recommending cumulative cause-specific hazards or multistate models instead, and holds up one study that used a landmark at seven days after intubation, time-dependent exposure covariates and two cause-specific hazard functions for death and discharge as addressing all three biases.

future_research.gap: Incomplete or unclear description of methods in the reviewed publications could have led to incorrect interpretation of what was done.
future_research.quote: Another limitation is that an incomplete or unclear description of the study methodology or/and results in the investigated publications could have resulted in incorrect interpretation of the analyses.

problems.evidence: In hospitalized patients, discharge competes with in-hospital death and is affected by treatment, and one study of eleven handled it. The review's recommended remedy is a full competing risk analysis giving cause-specific models for the event of interest and for every competing event, and it discourages Kaplan-Meier plots in this setting as liable to mislead, which places the standard visual summary of these studies among the sources of error.
problems.quote: Only one out of 11 studies addressed competing event bias by extending follow-up beyond patient discharge.

problems.evidence: Eight of the eleven had treatments that begin during the hospital stay, and none of those adjusted the primary hazard ratio for the resulting immortal time. This is a literature published in the four highest-profile general medical journal families under time pressure during a pandemic, so the failure occurred where scrutiny was greatest and the results carried furthest.
problems.quote: Eight studies had a time-dependent treatment. However, the hazard ratios were not adjusted for immortal time in the primary analysis.

problems.evidence: The review's final recommendation is that corrected estimates be reported as primary findings in the primary results section, which implies that presenting the corrected analysis as a secondary or sensitivity result is current practice. Where the corrected and uncorrected analyses answer differently, the choice of which occupies the abstract determines what the study is taken to have found.
problems.quote: Finally, corrected estimates should be reported as primary findings in the primary results section.

papers.title: Conducting Real-world Evidence Studies on the Clinical Outcomes of Diabetes Treatments.
papers.one_line: Sets out a three-layer framework for real-world evidence studies in diabetes, design, measurement and analysis, with target trial thinking at the design layer and full implementation transparency as the requirement for reproducibility.
papers.what_was_done: The review integrates practice for conducting and reviewing real-world evidence studies of diabetes treatments across three layers. The design layer is driven by the study question and refined by a medically informed target population, patient-informed outcomes and biologically informed effect windows, with the recommendation to imagine the randomized trial one would ideally run before designing the study in its likeness, and with the new-user active-comparator cohort design identified as the workhorse. The measurement layer transforms a longitudinal patient-level data stream into the variables identifying the population, pre-exposure characteristics, treatment and treatment-emergent outcomes, and the review notes that working with secondary data is more complex here than the primary collection typical of trials. The analysis layer concentrates on causal effect estimation, with propensity score methods for confounding, and names investigator errors to avoid: immortal time bias, adjustment for causal intermediates and reverse causation. It assesses what diabetes data sources record adequately, dispensing well but insulin dosing unreliably, endpoints through hospitalization codes, glycemic control through laboratory results, and it names data leakage in electronic records, the absence of any standard for what records should contain, and heterogeneity between systems. It ends by quoting a caution that formal analyses can serve only as thought experiments within informal guidelines.

future_research.gap: There is no universal standard for what electronic health records should contain, so between-system heterogeneity and incompleteness have to be accommodated study by study.
future_research.quote: there is no universally adopted standard for the types of data that should constitute EHRs, resulting in heterogeneity between EHR systems

problems.evidence: Fitness of the data for the question is stated as an essential point and is then assessed variable by variable through clinical judgment: dispensings recorded well, insulin dosing unreliable, confounders assessable reasonably well through direct or proxy measurement. There is no threshold anywhere in the framework at which a data source would be declared unable to support a given target trial, and the review notes that some lack of methodological rigor has been observed in this literature.
problems.quote: The underlying data need to be fit-for-purpose to answer the specific question at hand

problems.evidence: The review names full implementation transparency as the condition for reproducible findings and offers it as a requirement rather than as something the field currently delivers. Registries are singled out: because no standard definitions exist, a reviewer must examine how the data were generated and needs reach-through capability to the raw data, which the review notes some journals have begun to require.
problems.quote: To increase reproducibility of RWE findings, studies require full implementation transparency.

problems.evidence: The confidence argument offered for causal conclusions in this field is that real-world evidence has both replicated and predicted trial findings, which transfers credibility from a set of successful replications to the design as such. The review immediately conditions it on correct implementation and closes with a quotation stating that complete causal modeling is prohibited by the complexity of medical context and that formal analyses serve only as thought experiments.
problems.quote: instills confidence that causal conclusions can be reached from RWE in diabetes if implemented correctly

papers.title: Educational note: addressing special cases of bias that frequently occur in perinatal epidemiology.
papers.one_line: Catalogues the biases peculiar to perinatal epidemiology, including live-birth bias for which the note states no correction method exists, because the data needed to identify common causes of pregnancy loss cannot be obtained.
papers.what_was_done: Pregnancy is a time-limited period with severe cohort attrition between conception and birth, and the note works through the resulting biases: fixed cohort bias from the delimited duration of pregnancy, selection of live births, conditioning on potential intermediates, treatment of race and ethnicity, and prolonged, seasonal or time-varying exposures. Live-birth bias is given two mechanisms. Under the collider structure it requires that the exposure be related to pregnancy loss and that a second variable related both to loss and to the outcome exists, opening a noncausal path through the conditioned loss and an unmeasured common cause. Under depletion of susceptibles the exposure preferentially causes loss of fetuses more susceptible to the outcome. Either could be addressed statistically with data on pregnancy loss or on all common causes, and the note states that accurate data on loss including the weeks after implantation exist only in small studies with daily hormonal measurement, that no study can guarantee complete information on the common causes, and that no correction method exists in their absence. It adds that not all conceptions are clinically detectable, so the common causes cannot be measured under any design, and that redefining the target population as all conceptions is not necessarily meaningful. Fixed cohort bias, by contrast, has straightforward solutions.

future_research.gap: More studies of pregnancy loss are needed to identify the common causes of loss and adverse birth outcomes, and even then adequate control may not be feasible.
future_research.quote:
Whereas live-birth bias likely

results in underestimation of harmful effects, more studies on pregnancy loss are required to help identify common causes of pregnancy loss and adverse birth outcomes.

problems.evidence: Restricting to live births is not a choice an analyst makes but a condition of observing the outcome at all, and it conditions on a variable affected by the exposure and sharing unmeasured causes with the outcome. The note states that no method exists to correct it without data that cannot be obtained, and that even with the measurable common causes and methods accounting for survivor bias, adequate control may not be feasible.
problems.quote: To date, to the best of our knowledge, no method exists to correct for livebirth bias in the absence of this information, and often— e.g. when studying effects of environmental exposures on neurodevelopmental outcomes—the outcome can only be observed in live births.

problems.evidence: The variable that would have to be measured, pregnancy loss including in the weeks after implantation, is recorded only in select small studies with daily hormonal measurement, and many conceptions are never clinically detected. So the quantity is not merely unmeasured in routine data but unmeasurable at population scale, which sets a limit on any bias analysis that would need its distribution.
problems.quote: However, accurate data on pregnancy loss, including in the weeks after implantation, are only available in select small studies with detailed information on daily hormonal levels,16 and no study can guarantee complete information on all potential common causes of pregnancy loss and outcome of interest.

problems.evidence: The note observes that even after adjusting for live-birth bias the estimated parameter may not have a direct link to real-world outcomes, and that redefining the target population as all conceptions rather than live births is not necessarily meaningful. The estimand that a correction produces is therefore not automatically the one the question was about, and the note's remedy is to state the question and the identifiability assumptions up front rather than to select a target.
problems.quote:
For example, adjusting analyses for live-birth bias arising because
of the cohort attrition between conception and birth can
be infeasible in many studies and complicated, at best, in
others; even after adjustment, the estimated parameter
may not have a direct link to the real-world outcomes.

papers.title: Multidisciplinary tumor boards and their analyses: the yin and yang of outcome measures.
papers.one_line: Commentary showing that a reported survival benefit from more tumor board discussions is immortal time bias, since being discussed more often requires living longer.
papers.what_was_done: A published matched-pair analysis of 454 patients across 66 tumor types had compared response and overall survival between patients whose cases were discussed at multidisciplinary tumor boards and those whose were not, finding that only patients with more than three board discussions had significantly better overall survival, with no difference in response, relapse-free survival or time to progression, and no difference for any specific tumor type. The commentary, written with statisticians specializing in cancer data, concludes the result is deceiving: patients must survive long enough to be discussed more often, so the number of discussions encodes survival. It sets the finding in a general principle quoted from the methodological literature, that comparing a primary outcome among patients defined by another outcome such as dose intensity, compliance or adverse event experience, using standard approaches measuring outcome from the start of treatment, is statistically invalid. It draws the practical conclusion that the result should not be read as showing more board meetings automatically increase survival, and observes that of the 19 authors of the commented paper, no statistician appears to have been involved.

problems.evidence: The commentary generalizes beyond tumor boards to a class of analyses: any comparison of survival among groups defined by another outcome realized during follow-up, whether dose intensity, adherence or adverse events, measured from the start of treatment, is invalid by the same structure. That covers a large share of the observational literature on treatment markers, and the invalidity is in what the groups mean rather than in the estimator.
problems.quote: “Analysis of survival by tumor response and similar analyses in which the primary outcome is compared among patients defined by some other outcome (dose-intensity, compliance to treatment, adverse event experience) using standard statistical approaches measuring outcome from the start of treatment are statistically invalid”.

problems.evidence: The count of board discussions is a cumulative exposure that can only increase with survival, so the group with more than three discussions is defined by having lived long enough to accumulate them. The commentary notes that the only significant result in the original analysis was for that group, which is exactly what the bias predicts, and that no difference appeared for any of the outcomes not tied to duration.
problems.quote: Here patients need to survive long enough to be discussed more often.
